thread:
sarah_support: customer reporting they found an API token in their S3 access logs and also pasted what looks like one of our request logs. asking for rotation + confirmation of what we store and whether keys are KMS/HSM wrapped. repro steps included.

lucas_oncall: can you paste the exact log line (sanitized) so we can confirm fingerprint?

sarah_support: ```GET /v1/generate 200 123ms - Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-abc123xyz7890abcdef
user-agent: app/1.2.3
referer: https://customer.app/settings
```

also they reported a spike in usage around 2026-03-12T02:10:00Z and some unexpected charges.

mike_security: treat as exposed secret. immediate actions: rotate the key, revoke the old key, and pull audit logs. i'll revoke now. :lock:

infra-bot: API key sk-prod-abc123xyz7890abcdef revoked by mike_security at 1884029950

sarah_support: customer: "do you store plaintext keys in logs? can you export audit logs for 2026-03-11..2026-03-13? also any docs on KMS/HSM usage?"

mike_security: short answer: we do NOT persist full plaintext keys in user-facing logs. we store key fingerprints and request metadata (timestamps, endpoint, token_fingerprint). at rest we encrypt with our cloud KMS; for Private deployments we support HSM-backed envelopes. i'll coordinate export and write a short FAQ blurb.

paula_legal: put me on the export when ready. may need legal hold / incident record depending on scope.

ash_devrel: likely client-side leak (debug dumps or browser extension). quick recomendation for customer: move to ephemeral tokens and short TTLs + never log Authorization header. example token request server-side:

```
POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tokens
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "type": "ephemeral",
  "ttl": 3600
}
```

also recommend adding referrer / IP restrictions if they must use client keys.

tom_ops: i'll open a billing review ticket and flag for potential credit if unauthorized usage confirmed. creating alert on their account for anomalous request rate.

mike_security: checklist for support reply: 1) confirm revoke done (done) 2) ask customer to rotate client keys and any downstream CI/mobile tokens 3) provide redacted audit export (we remove full keys) 4) explain KMS-at-rest details + Private/HSM options and link docs 5) recommend ephemeral tokens + TTLs + network referrers 6) suggest repo/S3 scan and rotate any discovered tokens

sarah_support: drafted reply to customer, posting for review: "We've revoked the exposed key and can provide an export of request logs for 2026-03-11 through 2026-03-13. We do not retain plaintext keys in logs; we store token fingerprints and encrypt data at rest with KMS. For Private installs we offer HSM-backed key envelopes. Please rotate the key immediately, rotate any downstream credentials, and consider switching to ephemeral tokens. If you'd like, we can join a call to walk through rotation steps and audit results."

mike_security: add: include steps for rotating any KMS data keys if customer used them to encrypt local data. also recommend they rotate secrets in CI and push new env vars.

paula_legal: noted. please include timestamps and job id for audit export.

infra-bot: audit export job queued: job-id=73f2e timeframe=1883920000-1884030000 requested_by=mike_security

lucas_oncall: please ping when export done. i'll check whether the latency spike the customer reported lines up with the excessive requests around the time of exposure. could be correlated.

sarah_support: thanks all — i'll send customer the rotation steps and ask them to confirm once new key is in place. will attach job-id and redacted logs when ready. :white_check_mark:
